items.title: Game Boy Color on My Conference Badge
items.text: Game Boy Color on My Conference Badge I'm at GitHub Universe this week and, similar to last year , the conference badge is a full-blown color screen computer. I've been hacking around with it again, and then I ran into with Steve Francia... who worked with Gemini to get a full NES emulator working on it, and then went a step further and deployed an emulator for both the Game Boy and the Game Boy Color. Which means, if you can obtain the ROM, you can run The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening on your conference badge! A neat feature of the badge is that you can turn it upside down and then use game controller touch buttons that are built into the badge body. Tags: games , github , hardware-hac

items.title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
items.text: Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer. It uses open-weight models (currently Gemma 4 and gpt-oss). All your chats and files never leave your system. The only things that go online are web search (can be turned off in settings) and any MCP connectors you add yourself. Main features: - Automatically finds the best open-weight model for your hardware on first install (Mac/Linux/Windows) - Writes sandboxed Python code for ad hoc tools (data processing
